abstract.t: This document specifies the DTN Basket Protocol, a binary application schema based on CBOR (RFC 8949) designed for the aggregation, multi-requesting, and synchronous/asynchronous transfer of resources in delay-tolerant networks (DTNs) utilizing the Bundle Protocol Version 7 (RFC 9171). The protocol separates the control plane (structured metadata and CoAP statuses) from the data plane (raw content transmitted in distinct bundles).

section.name: Introduction
section.t: In disconnected or intermittent networks governed by the Bundle Protocol v7 (BPv7, ), reducing network overhead is critical. The DTN Basket Protocol allows the aggregation of multiple heterogeneous requests (retrieval, verification, search, cancellation, listing) within a single basket encoded in CBOR ().
To ensure data integrity under BPSec () while permitting partial responses by intermediary nodes, the protocol separates control and content:

ul.li: A CBOR control bundle (basket-response) carrying only metadata and application execution statuses.
Native BPv7 network bundles carrying the raw payloads of each resource.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 .

section.name: Protocol Specification (CDDL)
section.t: The exact syntactical structure of the request basket and the response envelope is defined below in CDDL ().

section.name: Detailed Method and Operation Semantics
section.t: The DTN Basket Protocol specifies five different operations denoted by the integer value in the op field (key 0) of each request-item in a basket. This section defines the precise operational logic, responder behavior, and expectations for each method.

section.name: GET (op=0) - Resource Retrieval
section.t: The GET operation is used to request the complete, raw payload of a specific resource identified by the uri field.
Upon receiving a successful GET request, the responder node MUST perform the following actions:

ul.li: Generate a control bundle carrying a basket-response mapping containing an item-response for this query with the coap-status-code set to 2.05 Content (69). The item-metadata MUST be populated with the SHA-256 hash (key 0), size (key 1), and MIME type (key 2) of the resource.

Emit a separate, native BPv7 bundle containing only the raw payload bytes of the resource in its payload block. This raw bundle MUST NOT contain any CBOR wrapper or application-level headers. The correlation between the control bundle and this raw data bundle is performed out-of-band by comparing the SHA-256 hash.

section.t: If the requested resource is not available on the responder, it MUST set the status code to 4.04 Not Found (132) and MUST NOT emit a data bundle.

section.name: CHECK (op=1) - Metadata Verification
section.t: The CHECK operation allows a requester to query metadata (such as existence, size, hash, or modification date) for a specified resource without transferring its actual content payload. This is highly useful for optimizing bandwidth in congested or expensive links.
The responder node MUST return the metadata in the control bundle (basket-response) using the item-metadata structure and set the status code to 2.05 Content (69).
The responder MUST NOT generate any raw data bundle for a CHECK operation.
If the resource does not exist, the responder MUST return the status code 4.04 Not Found (132).

section.name: SEARCH (op=2) - Multi-Resource Discovery
section.t: The SEARCH operation is used for discovering multiple matching resources based on criteria specified in the uri field (such as tags, wildcard paths, or keyword filters).
When processing a SEARCH request, the responder node MUST perform the following actions:

ul.li: Find all matching resources in its local store. Let the number of matches be M.

Construct a single basket-response containing M individual item-response elements. Each of these response elements MUST set item_idx to the index of the original SEARCH query in the basket. Multiple item-response maps inside a basket-response array MAY share the same item_idx value when the search operation yields multiple matching resources for that query.
Generate a separate raw BPv7 bundle for each matched resource, totaling M data bundles.

section.t: To prevent traffic amplification attacks in bandwidth-constrained environments, the responder SHOULD enforce an upper limit of results M_max (e.g., M <= 50). If the number of matching resources exceeds M_max, the responder SHOULD NOT emit the individual data bundles. Instead, the responder SHOULD substitute the execution with a LIST operation (op=4) to return a single bibliographic index bundle.

section.name: CANCEL (op=3) - Pending Request Abort
section.t: The CANCEL operation aborts the processing and transmission of all bundles associated with a previously submitted request identified by the value in the uri field (which maps to the targeted req_id).

Intermediary store-and-forward nodes processing a CANCEL request MUST search their local queues for pending bundles matching the targeted req_id (both control bundles and data bundles) and purge them. They MUST also forward the CANCEL bundle downstream.

The final target node, if still processing the original request, MUST immediately abort execution and return a basket-response containing an item-response with the status code set to 2.02 Deleted (66). This response bundle MUST NOT be propagated further.

section.name: LIST (op=4) - Bibliographic Indexing
section.t: The LIST operation is designed to obtain a structured, lightweight index of resources matching the search criteria without transferring the individual resources.

The responder node MUST compile a single text document using the text/markdown format listing all matching resources. Each entry in the document MUST contain bibliographic fields formatted as an AsciiDoc-style front-matter block or key-value list including fields such as Title, Author, MIME, Size, POSIX Date, SHA-256 hash, and Page count (if applicable).
The responder MUST emit exactly two bundles:

ol.li: One control bundle containing a basket-response mapping with status 2.05 Content (69) referencing the compiled document's metadata.
One raw data bundle containing only the compiled text/markdown index document.

section.name: Payload-to-Metadata Correlation
section.t: Raw BPv7 data bundles carry no application-level headers, metadata, or CBOR encapsulation. Instead, receiving nodes MUST use the following correlation procedure to bind incoming unencapsulated data bundles to their corresponding request context:

ol.li: Upon receiving an unencapsulated data bundle, the receiver MUST compute the SHA-256 digest of the bundle's payload block.
The receiver MUST query its stored basket-response tables (or active request context) for an item-metadata entry where Key 0 (hash) matches the computed SHA-256 digest.
Upon a successful match, the data payload IS bound to the corresponding request identifier (req_id) and item index (item_idx).

section.name: Requester Operations
section.t: The sending node MUST assign a unique req_id. It MUST order the elements of the request-item array in descending order of priority (index 0 representing the highest priority).

section.name: Forwarder and Intermediary Node Operations
section.t: An intermediary node possessing in its local cache all or part of the requested resources MAY generate the corresponding response bundles. When responding partially:

ul.li: It MUST transmit the application bundle basket-response containing the resolved items to the reply_to or the BPv7 source.
It MUST forward the original basket-request bundle strictly unchanged to adjacent nodes to maintain BPSec integrity ().

section.name: Responder Operations and Lifetime Mapping
section.t: When generating a response bundle (metadata or raw content), the responder MUST configure the Lifetime field of the BPv7 Primary Block according to the following order of precedence:

ol.li: The value of the item.lifetime field (key 6) if defined.
The value of the basket-request.default-lifetime field (key 3) if defined.
The default configuration of the local responder node.

section.name: CoAP Status Codes Mapping
section.t: The coap-status-code field of the item-response component MUST use the registry defined by RFC 7252 . The following codes are defined by this specification:

tr.td: Success for GET, CHECK, SEARCH, LIST

section.name: Amplification Attacks
section.t: The SEARCH operation (op=2) presents a traffic amplification risk (transmission of 1 + M bundles). Responder nodes SHOULD impose a maximum result limit (e.g., M <= 50). Beyond this limit, the responder SHOULD substitute the execution with a LIST operation (op=4) and return a single report.

section.name: Content Correlation and Verification
section.t: The receiving node MUST validate the integrity of each raw content bundle received separately by computing its SHA-256 hash and comparing it with field 0 of the item-metadata structure transmitted in the basket-response bundle.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests the creation of three IANA registries/registrations:

ul.li: An entry in the CBOR Tags Registry for the DTN Basket application tag.
The registration of the MIME types application/dtn-basket-request+cbor and application/dtn-basket-response+cbor in the Media Types registry.
The creation of the DTN Basket Operations Registry for managing operation integers (0=GET, 1=CHECK, 2=SEARCH, 3=CANCEL, 4=LIST).

section.name: Scenario 1: Multi-Item Priority Request (GET and CHECK)
section.t: In this scenario, the requester submits a single basket requesting to verify the metadata of an APK patch (using CHECK) and retrieve a specific file content (using GET).
Conceptual JSON Basket Request:
CBOR Diagnostic Notation representing the request, wrapped in CBOR Tag 44444:
The responder processes the basket and returns a single basket-response containing status reports for both items.
Conceptual JSON Basket Response:
CBOR Diagnostic Notation representing the response, wrapped in CBOR Tag 44444:
Data Plane Transfer:

Exactly one raw content bundle is generated by the responder, carrying the payload bytes for the resource at dtn:cid:bafybeiccf2 (120,000 bytes). No raw bundle is generated for the CHECK operation on the APK patch.

section.name: Scenario 2: Bibliographic Index Request (LIST)
section.t: The requester wants to list available radio documentation relating to Yaesu FT-817 transceiver.
Conceptual JSON Basket Request:
CBOR Diagnostic Notation representing the request, wrapped in CBOR Tag 44444:
The responder generates a control bundle and compiles the index document in Markdown.
Conceptual JSON Basket Response:
CBOR Diagnostic Notation representing the response, wrapped in CBOR Tag 44444:
The content of the raw data bundle transmitted separately:

section.name: Scenario 3: Delta Synchronization with Hashes (SEARCH)
section.t: The requester searches for files tagged as "emergency-medical-guide" but already has two of the manuals. To prevent sending duplicate documents, the requester lists truncated 8-byte hashes of the manuals it already owns in have_hashes.
Conceptual JSON Basket Request:
CBOR Diagnostic Notation representing the request, wrapped in CBOR Tag 44444:

The responder matches 3 guides. Since 2 matches have truncated hashes matching those in have_hashes, the responder registers all 3 matches but only sends the raw payload bundle for the third guide (the new one).
Conceptual JSON Basket Response:
CBOR Diagnostic Notation representing the response, wrapped in CBOR Tag 44444:
Data Plane Transfer:
Only 1 raw data bundle containing Guide C (hash e5f6..., 180,000 bytes) is transmitted. No data bundles are transmitted for Guide A and B.
